recent_posts.title: From Concept to Deployment: Integration Process for Clearpath Robotics Platforms
recent_posts.summary: Clearpath Robotics outlines their structured integration process for adding sensors, payloads, and software to their mobile robot platforms (Warthog, Husky, Jackal, Ridgeback, Dingo, AMP). The process covers three levels of integration complexity: standard, complex, and engineering services. Each project follows a defined workflow: initial consultation, technical scoping, concept proposal, detailed design, and build/integration. Key engineering considerations include sensor placement, power budgets, networking architecture, mechanical constraints, ROS driver development, URDF modeling, and documentation for long-term maintainability.

recent_posts.title: Research Round-Up: Off-Road Autonomy and Multi-Robot Collaboration
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of recent academic research papers using Clearpath Robotics platforms in real-world experiments. Three projects are highlighted: TSEASL, a motion-planning approach tested on a Warthog robot navigating dense forests; an improved localization system for agricultural robots in citrus orchards using a Jackal with LiDAR; and SwarmBuild, a decentralized multi-robot system where Husky ground robots and aerial drones collaboratively map and construct structures in GPS-denied environments.

recent_posts.title: Warthog: A Rugged Platform for Industrial Automation
recent_posts.summary: Warthog UGV is an all-terrain unmanned ground vehicle from Clearpath Robotics built for industrial and research use. It supports 272 kg payload, reaches 18 km/h, and is rated IP65. The platform ships with ROS 2 preinstalled and a Gazebo simulation model for virtual testing. Key use cases include mining inspection, precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, and robotics R&D. Optional OutdoorNAV software enables waypoint navigation and autonomous route execution across unstructured outdoor environments.

recent_posts.title: How to Connect Your Clearpath Robot to Wi-Fi
recent_posts.summary: Step-by-step guide for connecting Clearpath robotic platforms to Wi-Fi networks. Covers accessing the onboard computer via ethernet (192.168.131.1), establishing SSH connection, configuring Netplan YAML files with wireless interface settings, SSID and password, and verifying internet connectivity. Includes platform-specific instructions for Husky, Warthog, Jackal, Dingo, and Ridgeback robots, plus troubleshooting tips for common connection issues.

recent_posts.title: How to Choose the Best Clearpath Platform For Your Project
recent_posts.summary: Clearpath Robotics offers multiple robotic platforms for different environments and use cases. Indoor platforms include TurtleBot 4 (education), Dingo (compact research), and Ridgeback (heavy payload). Outdoor platforms include Jackal (versatile, indoor/outdoor), Husky (flagship medium platform), and Warthog (largest, heavy-duty). Key selection criteria include operating environment, payload capacity (9-272 kg), speed (0.31-2.0 m/s), runtime (2.5-15 hours), and terrain requirements. All platforms support custom sensor integration including LiDARs, cameras, manipulator arms, and various drivetrain configurations. Clearpath provides engineering support for platform selection and system customization.

recent_posts.title: ROS 2 Support: Platforms, Sensors, and Getting Started
recent_posts.summary: ROS 2 Humble and Jazzy are now supported across most Clearpath robotic platforms (Warthog, Husky, Jackal, Ridgeback, Dingo) on amd64 architectures, with arm64 support coming soon. The platforms support common sensors including 2D/3D lidars, IMUs, GPS, and cameras. Clearpath provides customized Ubuntu ISOs (22.04 for Humble, 24.04 for Jazzy) with automated firmware updates and installation scripts. Comprehensive tutorials cover velocity commands, movement control, and sensor integration to help users get robots operational quickly.

recent_posts.title: 2025 Round-Up: Husky A300, Partnerbot, and Community
recent_posts.summary: Clearpath Robotics launched the Husky A300 mobile robot platform with enhanced power, payload capacity, and flexibility based on customer feedback. The company also introduced the Husky AMP variant with integrated sensors and autonomy software for faster development. Through the PartnerBot Grant Program, they allocated over $100,000 to support robotics research in wildfire protection, sustainable farming, lunar exploration, and AI navigation. The team participated in major robotics conferences including ICRA in Atlanta, Actuate in San Francisco, and ROSCon in Singapore.

recent_posts.title: Best Robotics Conferences and Events to Attend in 2026
recent_posts.summary: A curated list of major robotics conferences scheduled for 2026, including NVIDIA GTC (March, San Jose), European Robotics Forum (March, Norway), Robotics Summit and Expo (May, Boston), ICRA (June, Vienna), RoboBusiness (Santa Clara), ROSCon (September, Toronto), and IROS (September, Pittsburgh). Each event focuses on different aspects of robotics research, development, and industry applications, offering opportunities for networking, learning about emerging trends, and connecting with researchers and industry leaders.

recent_posts.title: Inside the ROAS Global Robotics Forum: How Clearpath Robots Are Powering Research in South Korea
recent_posts.summary: The ROAS Global Robotics Forum in South Korea showcased four research projects using Clearpath Husky platforms with Franka manipulator arms. Projects demonstrated human-robot collaborative manipulation with object parameter estimation, task-aware semantic planning using GNN-Transformer architecture for natural language instructions, whole-body control using Hierarchical Quadratic Programming with self-collision avoidance, and multi-arm coordination for object retrieval and packing in cluttered environments. The research highlights advances in autonomous manipulation, perception systems, and intelligent decision-making for mobile manipulators.

recent_posts.title: Choosing Your TurtleBot 4: Standard vs Lite
recent_posts.summary: Comparison guide between TurtleBot 4 Standard and Lite models for robotics development. The Standard version includes a sensor tower with 2D LiDAR, OAK-D-Pro camera, UI board, and expansion capabilities, making it suitable for advanced research and custom applications. The Lite version offers core mobility and vision features at a lower cost with simpler setup, ideal for learning ROS 2 fundamentals, mapping, and navigation. Both platforms run ROS 2 and support autonomous navigation projects.
